data.name: Shashidhar
data.gender_notes: Shashidhar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Lord Shashi is the god of knowledge and wisdom. He is the god who imparts knowledge to students and scholars. He is also known as the god of learning, wisdom and intellect. The name Shashidhar carries the meaning “God of Knowledge” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Shashidhar usually hope their child will grow to embody god of knowledge and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Lord Shashi is a spiritual symbol of knowledge and wisdom. He represents the power of the mind and the ability to gain knowledge and understanding through study, meditation and self-reflection.
data.etymology: Shashidhar belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Knowledge.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shashidhar total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_sanskrit.name: शशिधर

data.cultural_impact: The name "Shashidhar" holds significant cultural value in Hinduism as it refers to Lord Shashi, who is considered as the patron deity of learning and wisdom. The name is deeply rooted in Indian culture, where education and knowledge are held in high esteem. Individuals bearing the name "Shashidhar" are often seen as intellectually gifted or possessing deep knowledge in their respective fields. This cultural association with Lord Shashi strengthens the value of education and knowledge in society.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name "Shashidhar" carries deep significance as it represents the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom, which is considered a essential step towards realizing the ultimate truth or dharma. The name instills in the bearer a sense of responsibility to constantly learn and grow, both for their personal well-being and for the betterment of society. The spiritual connection to Lord Shashi, who is the embodiment of knowledge and wisdom, serves as a reminder of the importance of knowledge in one's spiritual journey towards self-realization and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shashidhar: One who possesses truth and righteousness in every thought and deed. Embodiment of sincere promise and commitment to dharma.
